coauthors.name: Shaina Raza
coauthors.affiliation: Vector Institute for Artificial Intelligence, Toronto, ON, Canada (also listed as Toronto Metropolitan University on 2404.01399)
coauthors.relevance_evidence: Senior author on all four of Ghuge's papers and lead author of HumaniBench (arXiv 2505.11454), an explicit human-VALUES alignment benchmark for large multimodal models: 'their alignment with human centered (HC) principles such as fairness, ethics, inclusivity, empathy, and robustness is often overlooked... a unified framework for characterizing HC alignment across realistic, socially grounded visual contexts... All models show persistent gaps in fairness and multilingual inclusivity.' Also senior author of LinguaMark (arXiv 2507.07274), a cross-lingual fairness/bias benchmark over 11 languages and five social attributes, and of 'She had Cobalt Blue Eyes: Prompt Testing to Create Aligned and Sustainable Language Models' (arXiv 2310.18333) whose stated aim is that 'LLM outputs uphold the ethical standards of society'. Passes the gate on value alignment plus cross-lingual evaluation, not merely generic bias mitigation.

coauthors.name: Veronica Chatrath
coauthors.affiliation: Vector Institute, Toronto, ON, M5G 1M1, Canada (printed in the author footnote of 2310.00347: 'O. Bamgbose, V. Chatrath, S. Ghuge, and Y. Sidyakin are with the Vector Institute')
coauthors.relevance_evidence: First author of 'She had Cobalt Blue Eyes: Prompt Testing to Create Aligned and Sustainable Language Models' (arXiv 2310.18333), squarely a value-alignment paper: 'Appropriate safeguards must be in place to ensure LLM outputs uphold the ethical standards of society... This motivates our research question: how do we ensure LLM alignment? In this work, we introduce a test suite of unique prompts to foster the development of aligned LLMs that are fair, safe, and robust.' BORDERLINE NOTE for audit: the values dimension is societal/ethical alignment of LLMs rather than explicitly cross-cultural; no cross-cultural comparison in her record.

coauthors.name: Oluwanifemi Bamgbose
coauthors.affiliation: AI Engineering, Vector Institute for Artificial Intelligence, Toronto, M5G 1M1, Ontario, Canada
coauthors.relevance_evidence: Co-author of 'She had Cobalt Blue Eyes: Prompt Testing to Create Aligned and Sustainable Language Models' (arXiv 2310.18333, with Chatrath and Raza), which asks 'how do we ensure LLM alignment?' and tests whether LLM outputs 'uphold the ethical standards of society'. Same BORDERLINE caveat as Chatrath: societal/ethical value alignment in LLMs, no explicit cross-cultural axis. Her other work (MBIAS, Unlocking Bias Detection) is generic bias mitigation and would not pass on its own.

coauthors.name: Deval Pandya
coauthors.affiliation: Vector Institute for Artificial Intelligence, Toronto, ON, Canada (VP AI Engineering)
coauthors.relevance_evidence: Senior/last author on HumaniBench (arXiv 2505.11454), the human-centric VALUES alignment benchmark: 'alignment with human centered (HC) principles such as fairness, ethics, inclusivity, empathy, and robustness'; findings report 'persistent gaps in fairness and multilingual inclusivity'. BORDERLINE NOTE for audit: he is an institutional senior author (VP of AI Engineering at Vector) rather than a topic specialist; his remaining record (MLHOps, FAIR Enough, soft-prompt bias evaluation) is generic responsible-AI and would not pass on its own.

coauthors.name: Deepak John Reji
coauthors.affiliation: Computer Science Department, University of Limerick, Castletroy, V94 T9PX, Limerick, Ireland
coauthors.relevance_evidence: Author of 'LLM-Agent-based Social Simulation for Attitude Diffusion', which uses LLM agents to model social belief and value dynamics: 'simulate how public attitudes toward immigration change over time in response to salient events... this approach integrates multidimensional sociological belief structures and real-world event timelines... purpose-built as a social science research instrument specifically for studying attitude dynamics, polarisation, and belief evolution.' BORDERLINE NOTE for audit: this is social attitudes / sociological belief structures in LLM agents rather than 'cultural values' named as such; his other work (NBIAS, Dbias, accent speech synthesis) is generic bias/fairness and does not pass.
